<!--
  Thank you for contributing to Neovim!
  If this is your first time, check out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests-prs
  for our PR guidelines.
-->

## Problem
Closes #39239 
restart cmd don't reset the cwd to where it startup, and don't drop the `[file]` arguments when pass parameter to new process.
## Solution
Add a global var `initialdir` store the directory and pass it at `channel_job_start`, use `if(strequal(...))` to match options that need value right behind it to filter `[file]`(as maintainer pointed out in the issue, it duplicate the scan `command_line_scan` have done, but i didn't work it out how to leverage that. Need some advice here.)
### AI assistance
Generate part of test file

2) CICD fail in an unrealted test in Windows `test/functional/terminal/window_spec.lua` ,  and i can't reproduce on my Windows device, The failure is just a +1 line screen shift (content is identical), so it looks flaky, but I'm not sure

Then github will link to this PR from the issue.

Wanna some feedback about https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/39239#issuecomment-5268192336, do you insist that we shouldn't introduce these two states? Put `argv_is_file` aside, i think we should at least introduce `initialdir` to settle this down, spawn the process at a stable and predictable directory, no matter what form the `initialdir` variable takes, whether it's a plain global or tucked away in some static context @justinmk

~~`initialdir` is probably needed, it looks like we don't store it anywhere already.~~

~~`argv_is_file` looks like a hack~~

see comment below...

Since https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41304 , the restarted Nvim will gain the global CWD which may have changed after startup. That actually seems like the desired/intuitive behavior. And if so, then the only remaining work to do is to either (1) drop all `[file]` args, or (2) force them to absolute paths in the initial startup, so that they don't depend on the initial CWD.
